syllabus.clause: binary encoding (field-name dictionary + self-describing value) vs JSON strings vs inferred structs; parse_json, variant_get, path extraction; shredding frequently accessed fields into typed Parquet columns (GA in 4.1: faster reads, slower writes); interop with Parquet/Iceberg v3/Delta variant (cross-ref §6.2/§6.3).

at.step: Reveal: semi-structured data used to force a choice between two bad options
Predict: extracting one field, over and over. Faster from a JSON string, or from VARIANT?
Reveal: slower from the JSON string, measured directly
Elaborate: VARIANT is self-describing binary, not text
Predict: a field whose type varies row to row, cast into a fixed struct. Does every row survive?
Reveal: the mismatched row quietly becomes NULL, measured directly
Elaborate: a struct picks one type per field before any data arrives
Reveal: shredding buys the struct's own speed back, for the fields that earn it

items.item: VARIANT is GA with shredding for faster reads on semi-structured data, plus recursive CTE support and new approximate data sketches (KLL and Theta)

items.item: VARIANT itself (not shredding) was already usable in Spark 4.0, this chapter's own pinned version, under a preview/non-default flag -- shredding specifically, and VARIANT being on by default, are what SPARK-54454 GA'd in 4.1; the type's binary encoding and parse_json/variant_get this topic measures were already real and usable in 4.0.1.

at.out: VARIANT's own 4.0 availability versus its 4.1 GA and default-on status, named only; this topic's own examples.py measures parse_json/variant_get against 4.0.1 directly, where both already work

items.item: variant_explode flattens a VARIANT array or object into multiple rows, similar in spirit to explode() on an ArrayType column, but operating on a VARIANT's own internal structure rather than a statically-typed Spark collection.

at.out: variant_explode named only as a related function; this topic's own examples.py uses variant_get for scalar path extraction, not array/object flattening

items.item: schema_of_variant returns the inferred SQL schema of a variant value as a string, which is one real way to discover a semi-structured dataset's actual shape before deciding whether a field is stable enough to shred or declare as a struct field.

at.out: schema_of_variant's own role in discovering a dataset's real shape named only; this topic's own examples.py constructs the mixed-type example by hand rather than discovering it from schema_of_variant

items.item: spark.sql.variant.allowDuplicateKeys controls whether parse_json tolerates a JSON object with the same key appearing twice (keeping the last one) rather than raising -- a parsing-leniency knob distinct from the try_* functions' error-vs-NULL behavior this topic measures.

at.out: the duplicate-key parsing config named only as a separate leniency knob; this topic's own examples.py doesn't construct JSON with duplicate keys

items.item: Variant path syntax follows a dotted/bracketed convention ($.field, $.array[0], $.field.nested) matching the same path grammar get_json_object and JSONPath-style extraction already use, so migrating a get_json_object expression to variant_get is mostly a function-name swap, not a new syntax to learn.

at.out: the shared path-syntax convenience for migration named only; this topic's own examples.py uses the simplest single-field path ($.x, $.user_id) in both the JSON-string and VARIANT cases

items.item: Parquet's own VariantShredding.md specification (referenced directly in VariantSchema.java's own documentation comment) defines shredding at the file-format level, meaning a shredded VARIANT column is readable by any Parquet reader that implements the spec, not only by Spark.

at.out: shredding's cross-engine Parquet-spec-level portability named only; this topic's own examples.py doesn't test reading a shredded file from a non-Spark reader

items.item: Interop with Iceberg v3 tables requires the table itself to be created as a v3 table before a VARIANT column can be added, since the VARIANT type was introduced specifically in the Iceberg v3 table-format spec, not retrofitted onto v1/v2 tables.

at.out: the Iceberg v3 table-version requirement for VARIANT columns named only; this topic's own examples.py reads and writes plain Parquet files, not an Iceberg table

items.item: spark.sql.variant.pushVariantIntoScan, when enabled, lets a variant_get extraction be pushed down into a compatible data source's own scan (such as a shredded Parquet reader resolving straight to the typed column), rather than extracting after the full VARIANT value has already been read.

at.out: variant-extraction scan pushdown named only; this topic's own examples.py measures unshredded VARIANT extraction, where there is no typed column for a pushdown to resolve to

items.item: A VARIANT value has a documented size limit (enforced via VariantSizeLimitException in the same source module this topic quotes), meaning an unbounded or deeply nested JSON payload can fail parse_json outright rather than silently truncating -- a failure mode distinct from the struct-cast NULL-on-mismatch this topic measures.

at.out: the VARIANT size-limit exception as a distinct failure mode from the struct-cast case named only; this topic's own examples.py uses small, well under any size-limit payloads

items.item: Delta Lake's own variant-type support mirrors Iceberg's version-gating pattern: a Delta table needs the relevant table feature (variantType-preview or its successor) enabled before a VARIANT column can be written to it, matching how Parquet and Iceberg each gate the same capability behind a format or table-version requirement.

at.out: Delta's table-feature gating for VARIANT columns named only, as the same pattern Iceberg v3 and Parquet's own shredding spec use; this topic's own examples.py writes plain Parquet, not a Delta table
